plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'Permanent dentition showing severe dental erosion in a 40-year-old woman, suffering from an eating disorder for 20 years, including bulimia nervosa with self-induced vomiting. (A) Frontal view'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal intraoral clinical photograph of a 40-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa and self-induced vomiting, showing severe dental erosion (perimylolysis), a classic direct manifestation of bulimia nervosa. Caption explicitly attributes the finding to bulimia nervosa. B: Maxillary occlusal intraoral clinical photograph of the same patient with bulimia nervosa and self-induced vomiting, showing severe dental erosion of the upper dentition (perimylolysis), a classic direct manifestation of bulimia nervosa. Caption explicitly attributes the finding to bulimia nervosa.

in_text_mentions: d Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) [5]. Many symptoms of these disorders imply a high risk for oral health, causing caries, loss of teeth, and dental erosion [6, 7] (Fig. 1.). The symptoms of a long-term ED (e.g., self-starvation, self-induced vomiting, rumination, and chewing on food without swallowing) often vary over time, and cumulatively, they comprise a high risk of poor oral health, causing great suffering and high costs for both the patient and society when untreated. panels.rationale: Intraoral clinical photo shows visible enamel loss consistent with perimylolysis. Caption states erosion of enamel due to acid reflux and in-text links figure 3 erosion to diagnosis of long-standing bulimia nervosa in a disease-focused bulimia article.

panels.figure_caption: Showing Erosion of enamel due to acid reflux
in_text_mentions: opsy was taken from the same. Biopsy showed features suggestive of squamous cell carcinoma which was well differentiated (Figure 2). On the basis of investigations and errosion of teeth enamel noted due to reflux acid errosion (figure 3), a diagnosis of long standing bulimia nervosa leading to squamous cell carcinoma of esophagus was established. The patient was initiated on 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin in view of sqamous cell carcinoma along with cognitive behavioural therapy and short serotonin reuptake inhibitors in view of bulimia nervosa and was discharged; she is doing well on follow up.
